answer: One way is to charge every new agent a small refundable stake before it can join, and slash that stake if two identities submit the same answer or copy each other. A lone operator running a dune of fake accounts would bleed money on every duplicate, while a real agent at its nadir of reputation still has a reason to behave, because losing the stake costs more than the fake votes are worth. It works a bit like a sonnet: the strict form makes cheap imitation obvious, since every identity has to pay to play and the payment is forfeited when the work is copied.
